items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: I, Paul Barnes, went with Jell-A-Roll-Martin.

ctx.x: Great kind of guy. Darnell Harris?

No. No, Darnell Harris, in fact Darnell Harris taken his place. Oh really? In Chicago. And you knew him too. Yeah, he went away to Paris, France with Wilbur. Oh, I love that. Wilbur to Paris. Simeon. Oh, Omar. Omar Simeon. Yeah, that was our read section. Well we had a good band and so I won't get off that, but the band broke up because we were supposed to go in the cotton club and King Oliver wanted too much money, so instead the band got Duke Ellington. And that's why King Oliver made his mistake, because his…
I see. That's how you got up with Jell-A. Yeah, that's how I got up with Jell-A-Roll-Martin. Because King Oliver's band broke up.

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: when you were traveling with Jelly Roll you'd play one night for white people and then the next? ... Another time, yeah, for colored people.

ctx.x: Up north, because most of the mixing with the whites and colored would be in Harlem. The white people would come up and mix with the colored people. But there wasn't many of the colored people who would go down there and mix with them. Very few colored people would go, or mix with them.
So like when you were traveling with Jelly Roll you'd play one night for white people and then the next?

Another time, yeah, for colored people. But the white people always mix more, they'd mix more with the colored people, then the colored people would mix with them. For some reason it looked like it always was like that, I don't know. I wonder why? I just don't understand how.
